subject: Proposal: progressive-term bridge with mid-year scale triggers
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@helionai.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion: capacity plan & term options

Hi Jasmine,

We're kicking off renewal planning for Helion. Current footprint has grown 3.8x year-over-year and engineering expects another doubling during Q4 if a new feature lands. Can you share options we should evaluate: multi-year commit vs. annual, a ramp schedule we can rely on, and an approach to mid-year scale triggers (so we don't hit throttling during go-live)? Also want to understand auto-renew implications and how co-terming with another vendor contract would work from an invoicing/tax perspective.

Attached a quick usage export for June. Happy to set a call next week — Priya (cc) will coordinate legal/finance availability.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Head of Platforms, Helion AI

Attachment: usage-jun2026.csv (csv stub, 1 file)

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@helionai.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@helionai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: capacity plan & term options

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the data and context.

High level options I'd suggest for evaluation (I'll put numbers behind these and share a worksheet):
- Hybrid multi-year (36 months) with staged committed buckets: higher guaranteed capacity in year 1, predictable staged increases in years 2–3 tied to defined scale triggers.
- Annual renewals with a true-up cadence and optional burst credits for short spikes; lower discount but more flexibility.
- Co-terming: we can align invoice dates but would recommend keeping the legal term independent to preserve renewal flexibility.

A couple of operational notes:
- Mid-year scale triggers can be defined as either %-over-commit sustained for N days (auto top-up) or pre-authorized burst capacity that transitions into committed capacity on a monthly true-up.
- Auto-renew: default is auto-renew with a 60-day opt-out window; we can extend that for enterprise agreements.

I propose a 30-minute call next Tue to walk through a tailored worksheet. Karthik, can you join to review pricing levers? I'll attach an outline with the call invite.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Initial-Renewal-Outline.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Renewal discussion: capacity plan & term options

Team — forwarding Sanjay's note and the outline. Draft pricing thoughts below; please update before I send the formal worksheet.

--- Internal notes (do NOT include Helion) ---
From the data: recent 90-day 95p token throughput ~120M tokens/day; projection for Q4 ramp to 240M tokens/day if feature ships.

Proposal (working):
- Preferred: 36mo hybrid term. Year 1: 12-month locked commit with 20% burst credits. Years 2–3: staged commit increases (year 2 +40% on trigger, year 3 +30% on trigger).
- Discount: 8% off list for 36mo; 4% for 24mo; none for annual.
- True-up: monthly usage true-up against committed; can settle quarterly if customer prefers.
- Invoicing: invoice annual up-front or quarterly invoicing with prepay credit. For co-terming request — recommend annual invoices aligned to their fiscal year but with our renewal date separate. Finance will handle consolidated billing guidance.
- SLAs/operational: include canary capacity during first 30 days of major launches; fallbacks to lower-latency model variants if capacity constrained.

Outstanding items: legal tweaks to auto-renew window (customer asked for 60 days — we can keep) and early termination remedy for capacity shortfall.

Connor: can you validate the cost model (pricing-model-v2.xlsx) and confirm this fits our margin targets? Marissa: confirm whether we can offer an extra 2% promo for go-live within 60 days.

Thanks,
Jasmine

Attachment: pricing-model-v2.xlsx (xlsx stub)

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@helionai.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@helionai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: progressive-term bridge with mid-year scale triggers (HLN-2026-045)

Sanjay / Priya — thanks for the call yesterday. Attached is our proposed worksheet and a redline summary of contract differences for the suggested structure. Highlights below:

1) Structure: 36-month hybrid term (committed + staged triggers)
   - Year 1: Committed baseline = 100M tokens/day (annual equivalent), invoiced quarterly. Includes 20% burst credits to cover launch spikes.
   - Year 2: Trigger = sustained >120% of baseline for 10 business days; on trigger, staged commit increases to baseline * 1.4 (40% uplift).
   - Year 3: Further staged increase to baseline * 1.7 if triggered in year 2 or via negotiated uplift.

2) Pricing & discounts
   - 36mo blended discount: 8% off list for committed tokens; burst usage billed at list with pre-purchased bundle pricing.
   - Early go-live promo: additional 2% off year 1 committed spend if launch verified within 60 days of signing (requires ops sign-off).

3) Auto-renew and co-terming
   - Auto-renew: Contract auto-renews for successive 12-month terms unless customer provides written opt-out 60 days before renewal.
   - Co-terming: We can align invoicing cycles to Helion's fiscal calendar for convenience; legal term will remain independent unless customer requests consolidated renewal dates (we will escalate to Legal for co-term amendments).

4) True-up and invoicing
   - Monthly usage true-up against committed buckets; settlement quarterly by default. Invoicing cadence: quarterly by default; annual prepay available on request.

5) Operational protections
   - Canary capacity and burst routing for first 30 days of a major launch.
   - SLA credit policy remains per the standard enterprise schedule; we will offer escalated support during the first 90 days post-launch.

Next steps:
- If this structure works, Priya, please confirm legal/finance readiness and any mandatory contract language from Helion.
- We'll issue the DocuSign envelope for the renewal worksheet + redlines once legal confirms language.

Attaching: HLN-Renewal-worksheet.xlsx, redwood-terms-diff.pdf

Warmly,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Jasmine — this looks pragmatic and addresses our key concerns. Two quick clarifications before we loop legal:

1) Invoicing cadence: we prefer quarterly invoices but need a clear true-up statement that any committed increases triggered mid-quarter are reflected in the next invoice rather than retroactively charged. Can you confirm that statement will be explicit?
2) Early go-live promo: confirm ops sign-off process and who at Redwood verifies the launch for the 2% promo. We need that to be an internal Redwood contact we can ping.

If those two items are clarified in the redline, we're ready to move to DocuSign. Priya will coordinate with our procurement and legal and expects to have comments within 72 hours.

Thanks — Sanjay
Head of Platforms, Helion AI
